readme_draft:
# Night Shift

*Six weeks, one street, 2 AM to 4 AM.*

<!-- add a hero image here: frame 07 (first oven light) works well, 1600 px wide -->

Night Shift is my BFA Photography thesis. For six weeks I walked the same 400 metres of
Kettle Lane every night between 2 AM and 4 AM and photographed what the street does when
nobody is watching it.

The question was simple: does a street have a personality when its people are gone?

## The short answer

It does, and it keeps a timetable. The bakery switches on its ovens at about 3:10 AM.
The bins go out at 3:40 AM and the street gets loud for eleven minutes. A fox crossed near
number 27 on 31 of the 42 nights I logged. In six weeks, 9 people walked the full street.

An empty street is never empty. It is working for somebody else.

## The work

- **48 frames**, picked from 2,100 exposures - indexed in [`frames/index.csv`](frames/index.csv)
- **Written thesis** - [Chapter 1: Method](chapters/01-method.md) and [Chapter 2: What the street does at night](chapters/02-findings.md)

<!-- add a 3-image strip here: frames 07, 19 and 48 -->

## How I worked

| Rule | What it meant |
|---|---|
| Same route, same time | Bakery to bus depot, every night, 2 AM to 4 AM |
| Available light only | One camera, one 35mm lens, no flash, no tripod. If the street was too dark, the frame was too dark. |
| Nothing staged | If a fox did not walk past, there is no fox in the picture |

I shot film for the first two weeks and switched to digital in week three: sodium street
lamps turned every roll orange. From then on white balance stayed at 2800K.

## See it

The 48 frames will be shown at the graduate show in the main hall, June 2026.
<!-- add the show dates, venue link and an online gallery link here -->

case_study.title: Night Shift - a six-week night photo essay
case_study.problem: My thesis asked whether a street has a personality when its people are gone, and how to show that honestly without staging anything.
case_study.approach: I walked the same 400 metres of Kettle Lane every night from 2 AM to 4 AM for six weeks, with one 35mm lens, no flash and no tripod. After two weeks of orange film under sodium lamps I switched to digital at a fixed 2800K. I logged sounds and movements next to every frame.
case_study.outcome: 2,100 exposures edited down to 48 frames, a written thesis in two chapters, and a finding I could prove from my own log: the street keeps a timetable - ovens at 3:10, bins at 3:40, a fox on 31 of 42 nights.

freelance_pitch: I shot Night Shift, a six-week documentary series on one street between 2 AM and 4 AM: 48 frames edited from 2,100, all in available light. If you need a quiet, observant series about a place, a night shift or a team at work, I can plan it, shoot it and edit it down to the frames that matter.
